chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from his two brothers, from their father, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from one of them (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the zakat of the land: when the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) or the Imam (peace be upon him) takes a share (qabala) by half, third, or quarter, the zakat is upon him, and there is no zakat upon the one who receives it, unless the owner of the land stipulates that the zakat is upon the recipient. If he stipulates, then the zakat is upon them. And today, there is no zakat upon the people of the land except upon whoever has something in his hand from what the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) granted.

Therefore, this report is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because the meaning of his saying 'and there is no zakat upon the recipient' is that there is no zakat upon him for all that emerges from the land, although he is obliged with the zakat of what accrues in his hand after the division. And that which indicates what we said is the report we preceded from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said in his hadith: 'And the tithe is not upon all that Allah brings out of it, but the tithe is upon you regarding what accrues in your hand after its division to you.'
Thus, this report is detailed (mufassal) and the other report is general (mujmal), and ruling with the detailed is more worthy than ruling with the general over the detailed.

As for what this hadith included of his saying (peace be upon him) 'and there is no zakat upon the people of the land today,' it means that today a concession has been granted today to whoever zakat is obligatory upon him, and the unjust ruler takes from him, that he may count it as zakat, although it is better to pay it again, because that is a wrong that was done to him. And that which indicates this concession is what was narrated...

key_terms.قَبَّلَهَا: To take a share/portion (specifically by the ruler)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat for land when the ruler takes a share of the produce?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distribution of agricultural tithe (ushr) when the ruler claims a share (qabala), establishing that the zakat obligation typically falls on the ruler unless the landowner stipulates otherwise. The text reconciles apparent contradictions by distinguishing between the general grant of land and the specific obligation of tithe on the produce remaining in the owner's hand after the ruler's share is taken. It further notes the scholarly permission for landowners to count the ruler's unjust exaction (sulṭān al-jāhir) toward their zakat, though paying it again is preferred to avoid complicity in injustice.
